answer: For N replicas with Byzantine bound f, quorum Q > (N+f)/2 forces any two quorums to share at least 2Q-N > f correct replicas, making malicious intersection impossible when f < N/3. Validators stake C slashed by S=αC on equivocation, while zero-knowledge verifiable delay proofs add latency T, so U_attack = p·G - (1-p)·S - c(T) < 0 for stake fraction β < 1/3. Unilateral deviation is unprofitable, yielding a robust Nash equilibrium; the protocol reaches an ivory summit only after every honest node finishes its cryptographic voyage through the delay chain.
